questions.question: 1. What is the time complexity of insertion at any point on an array?

explanations.a: Correct. Insertion at any point in an array requires shifting elements, resulting in O(N) time complexity in the worst case.
explanations.b: Incorrect. O(N^2) would involve nested iterations, which is not the case for a single insertion operation.
explanations.c: Incorrect. O(NLogN) is typical for efficient sorting algorithms, not for array insertion.
explanations.d: Incorrect. O(N) is the correct time complexity for insertion at any point in an array.

questions.question: 2. What is the space complexity of Dijikstra’s algorithm? (V is the number of vertices in the graph)

explanations.a: Incorrect. O(V) would only store information for vertices but not the adjacency information needed for the algorithm.
explanations.b: Correct. The space complexity of Dijikstra’s algorithm is O(V^2) when using an adjacency matrix to represent the graph, where V is the number of vertices.
explanations.c: Incorrect. O(log V) is too small to represent all the data structures needed for Dijkstra's algorithm.
explanations.d: Incorrect. O(V^2) is the correct space complexity of Dijkstra’s algorithm with adjacency matrix.

questions.question: 3. What is the order of time complexities of BellmanFord(B), Dijkstra's(D) and Floyd Warshall(F) Algorithms.

explanations.a: Incorrect. This ordering suggests Dijkstra's is slower than BellmanFord, which is not correct.
explanations.b: Incorrect. This ordering suggests BellmanFord is slower than Dijkstra's, which is not correct.
explanations.c: Incorrect. This ordering suggests Dijkstra's is slower than Floyd Warshall, which is not correct.
explanations.d: Correct. The time complexity of Floyd Warshall is O(V^3), Bellman Ford is O(EV), Dijkstra is O(V^2).
